title: Tata Consumer Products Ltd - 500800 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Consumer Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14% to about INR4,000+ crores-equivalent run rate; EBITDA up 18%, margin up 40 bps to 14%, net profit INR470 crores (+16%).
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% (INR700 crores added), EBITDA grew 18% with margin up 40 bps to 14%, and profit before tax rose 21%. Net profit reached INR470 crores (+16%), EPS INR4.75; adjusted EPS (excluding brand amortisation) was INR5.18. First half revenue grew 13%, EBITDA 18%, and adjusted EPS INR9.85 (+21%). India business grew 11% UVG in the quarter, with salt (+15% revenue) and growth businesses (+40%) offsetting flat tea/coffee revenue (-1%); India segment margin contracted on tea and salt input inflation. International (+7% reported, -2% constant currency) and non-branded (+12%) improved profitability, lifting overall segment margin by 50 bps; shipping disruption and Mundra port issue hit international volumes. Management reiterated FY27 margin expansion guidance of 50-70 bps and said tea and salt price increases should flow into P&L from Q3.

financial_highlights.value: INR4.75 reported; INR5.18 adjusted (Q2); INR9.85 adjusted (H1)

financial_highlights.change: Visibility now reported separately; combined A&P+visibility ~6.3-6.5% of sales

segments.name: India Salt
segments.commentary: Revenue up 15% to close to INR1,100 crores on 9% volume growth; H1 up 11%. Market share ~39.8-39.9%. Price moved INR30 to INR32 in May and a further INR2 in early October (reported figures pre-dated the second hike).

segments.name: India Tea & Coffee
segments.commentary: Revenue down 1% (flat volume) in Q2 vs Q1 revenue -4%; H1 about -3%. Management attributes weakness to weather, price increases and LPG disruption hangover; third-party industry value cited at about -6%.

segments.name: Growth businesses (India)
segments.commentary: Up 40% to close to INR1,400 crores and now 38% of India business. Sampann +57% (dry fruits and cold-pressed oils ARR above INR1,000 crores); RTD volume +34%, revenue +47%; H1 growth 43%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Close to INR1,300 crores, +7% reported and -2% constant currency. UK revenue -8% on heatwave; US +4%; Canada +8% constant currency; South Africa strong. Shipping and Mundra port disruption (10-12 days) hit Capital Foods and Organic India exports.

segments.name: Non-branded
segments.commentary: Up 12% (9% constant currency) on elevated base; soluble volume +21%. Robusta and Arabica softening pressures realisations; margin swings driven by seasonal plantation accounting.

segments.name: Starbucks (India, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue +15% with same-store sales growth for fifth successive quarter and ~10% traffic growth; 7 stores opened, total 505 stores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 margin expansion guidance of 50-70 bps reiterated; management said it remains aggressively focused on margin expansion.
Tea price increases of ~8-10% since Q1 (initial 7-8%, now 2-3% week-on-week) intended to cover tea inflation; full P&L effect expected from Q3.
Salt guidance: mid-single-digit volume growth and a couple of bps of price per year; INR2 hike in October.
Capital Foods and Organic India: 25-30% growth guided going forward; international expected to see some catch-up uplift in Q3.
Growth portfolio guided at ~30%+ growth for the next 2-3 years; tea and salt guided mid-to-high single digits.
India food and beverage EBITDA endeavour of 17-20% ballpark, expected in roughly the next 3 years, though oil at ~USD115 and packaging/freight swings are headwinds.
capex_capacity: Starbucks plans accelerated store openings after calibrated openings to reset business model; 505 stores at quarter end.
Sampann described as asset-light with no capex, supporting high ROCE.
AI deployment: ~1,600-1,700 salespeople on AI sales companion; target 100% coverage by December; AI leaf-grading across ~120 leaf types and AI bottle inspection at Himalayan factory.
Distribution: ~19 lakh+ direct-reach stores; ~4.5-4.6 million numeric outlets; expanding distribution further.
HoReCa run-rate ~INR200-225 crores across ~10,000 outlets; vending ~INR150 crores run-rate; third business ~INR250 crores run-rate with ~10,000 outlets.
demand_pricing: Tea: industry soft (third-party value about -6%); TCPL market share stable; pricing ~8-10% since Q1 vs tea inflation; peak buying under way ahead of North India season; competitive intensity described as low, with industry prices moving up.
Salt: value-added and premium salts growing 2x base salt; Tata Salt Plus launched; no slowdown after second price hike.

RTD: Tata Gluco Plus at INR10 price point, value growth ahead of volume due to mix (higher-value Gluco Plus) and price increases taken in sync with 2-3 large players; competitors moved INR10 to INR12.
Sampann: quick commerce growth broadly in line with leading QC player's growth; Sampann margin ~14-15%, up ~270-290 bps YoY.
Coffee: US coffee prices easing to ~3.10-3.15 from 3.30-3.50 last year; international realisations pressured by softer Robusta/Arabica.

qa_highlights.question: Tea procurement status, inflation and price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Procurement peak buying under way post-Puja; pricing of ~8-10% since Q1 covers tea inflation, with week-on-week increments now 2-3%. Margin recovery expected as pricing flows through.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year and exit margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Reiterated 50-70 bps FY expansion guidance; salt price hikes and tea pricing to restore margins; H2 margin expansion targeted YoY, not sequential, given seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Is salt volume growth driven by pre-buying or competitor weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied pre-buying; no slowdown after second price hike; market share up to ~39.8-39.9%; guidance remains mid-single-digit volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Non-branded margin outlook for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Solubles margin steady; plantation margin swings are seasonal from Q2 as biological crop accounting starts, so Q2 margin likely to sustain in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is Tata Consumer's India EBIT margin path to 17-18% realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management referenced 17-20% EBITDA ambition for Indian food and beverage in roughly 3 years, with oil and packaging/freight headwinds; Sampann and RTD dilutive to base but accretive over time, Capital Foods and Organic India ~50% accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI deployment a cost saving or revenue lever?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost takeout expected but seen as par for the course; the real gain is revenue via better lines per call in DSR calls. Frequency reduction for outlets ordering under twice a month is about redeploying sales resources, not cost saving.

risks_watch: Tea volumes: Q2 flat; management expects return to low-to-mid single-digit growth but competitive and weather risk remain.
Input cost inflation in tea, salt, packaging, freight and oil (~USD115 cited); tea and salt price increases must flow into India margins from Q3.
International recovery: UK heatwave impact (-8% revenue), shipping rerouting around the Middle East and Mundra port disruption; high comparable base.
Growth portfolio base effects: Sampann dry fruit and oil growth will cycle; RTD performance tied to INR10 price point competition.
Innovation pipeline: about two-thirds of launches survive; one-third are discontinued after review.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin recovery, with the pricing and portfolio story repeated throughout; specific numbers given on most questions. Tea volume and margin recovery answers were more qualitative, and management did not quantify H2 margin exit rate.
key_quotes: So overall, see, broadly, while tea volumes have been flattish, volumes value has been flattish, market share is stable.
We continue to guide salt for mid -single-digit volume, a couple of basis points of price, and that is what we remain committed to delivering.

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 margin expansion of 50-70 bps and 30%+ growth for growth categories over 2-3 years, plus 25-30% growth for Capital Foods and Organic India, backed mainly by price increases in tea and salt, Starbucks store openings and growth-category momentum rather than specified new capacity; no capacity additions or capex were quantified.
